comments.body:
Sorry for the long text but as there's no place to share a review of them, I'll add my experience here. Take some popcorns and enjoy...
I rented a room in a shared flat from NextGen for 8 months.
The first 6 months were very smooth. They let the current tenants organize visits and meet the new ones so I could meet them in person and discuss before moving in which was quite nice. Next Gen was more or less reactive, I didn't have to complain about that.
At some point, one of the tenants moved out so me and the second tenant left had to find a new person. We organized it ourselves and found someone we appreciated. But she only stayed for 2 months so we had to find somebody else and from then everything went downhill...
They usually gave us contacts from people who answered to the ad online. A girl visited and she was a nice match so we told her she would get the room and informed NextGen. 10 days passed and she never got an answer after multiple requests. I was contacted by NextGen over the phone to "just get some update from the apartment". During the call I got told that the agency needs the 3rd key to furnish the 3rd room available in our apartment and that a new roommate (Luka) will move-in in a month until the end of the lease.
It seemed quite surprising as they completely ignored the girl we found. Since we didn't know anything about this "Luka", we asked to meet him over a call or a visit before he moves in. The day after the call, the room was fully furnished (cardboard and plastics were left there). Then the day after, the second tenant and I get the following text: 
"Just for your information:
Today, the new roommate Luka will move into the apartment.
He is from *** and will stay in the apartment until the end of the lease."
That was a big surprise because first of all, instead of moving in September as said over the phone call, Luka is now moving on the same day we have been warned (less than 12h notice), without us meeting him in advance, as mentioned in the contract.
Second of all, this was all lies since, in the evening, 3 strangers entered our apartment and installed themselves in the free room. They presented themselves as Alex and 2 friends, who found the room on Airbnb, got the key from a key box in the mailbox and will stay for 3 days. 2 days later, they leave in the morning and 2 girls arrive in the evening. The next day, 3 cleaning people enter the apartment in the morning, while we are here. So in 3 days 8 people entered the apartment we live in without any notice, warning or explanation.
On top of this, as me and the second other tenant are living in the apartment full time, we had to buy all necessary material for a normal living, including: taxed trash bags, dish soap and dish washer tabs, toilet paper, oil, salt, pepper and so on... However, in the Airbnb ad, NextGen mentions that more than 40 amenities are included like those I mentioned above. So all this material was now being used by not one but 2 to 3 extra people daily without any compensation of the costs. And their answer to that was to put our stuff away, which we did at some point but we weren't informed in advance and I was gone for a weekend When I came back the toilet paper and my soap were empty.....
Also, the cleaning of the common spaces, which is not done by the cleaning company that came for the room, is more demanding for the second tenant and me since we are 2 cleaning for 4 to 5 people instead of 3 cleaning for 3. The cleaning company even complained about the cardboard and plastic left from the furniture to us.
It continued for a month until the famous Luka finally arrived...
In the end NextGen didn't seem to care at all and ignored all the problems of that situation so I decided to find a new tenant for my room and move out. 
They seem to be money makers and as long as they're happy you'll be fine but when they can find a way to make money you'll be ignored completely.. Definitely a horrible experience for me so I do not recommend them. On top of this, the prices aren't cheap at all (800 bucks for a 9m2 room in an old apartment without living room as it is considered as a room and used by a tenant). AVOID!
comments.author: False_Pizza4215
